# Ollama thinking capability and reasoning controls — facts

> Source-anchored units about Ollama thinking capability and reasoning controls: 9 across 4 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## How it works

- [statement] The `think` request field is supported on both /api/chat and /api/generate; when enabled, output separates reasoning from the answer, and `think: false` makes the model skip thinking and output content directly. (high confidence) — https://ollama.com/blog/thinking · keywords: Ollama thinking capability and reasoning controls · also: https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/thinking.md
- [statement] In streaming, thinking chunks arrive before answer chunks; a client detects the first `thinking` chunk to open a thinking section and switches to the answer when `message.content` arrives. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/thinking.md · keywords: Ollama thinking capability and reasoning controls · also: https://ollama.com/blog/thinking
- [statement] On Ollama 0.12+, thinking-capable models (qwen3 thinking variants, deepseek-r1, deepseek-v3.1) auto-enable thinking when `think` is unset; standard models such as qwen2.5 and llama3.2 do not. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/pull/4821/files · keywords: Ollama thinking capability and reasoning controls

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] gpt-oss uses named effort levels instead of booleans: /api/show example shows values ["low","medium","high"] with default "medium"; Spring AI documents that gpt-oss takes string levels and not boolean enable/disable. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/thinking.md · keywords: Ollama thinking capability and reasoning controls · also: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/pull/4821/files
- [statement] gpt-oss natively takes reasoning effort low, medium or high set in the system message (e.g. `Reasoning: high`), defaults to medium, and writes raw chain of thought on the `analysis` channel, which OpenAI says should not be shown to end users; this is why Ollama exposes gpt-oss as string levels rather than a boolean. (medium confidence) — https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/articles/openai-harmony · keywords: Ollama thinking capability and reasoning controls · also: https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/thinking.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Response fields: chat returns reasoning in `message.thinking` and the answer in `message.content`; generate returns `thinking` and `response`. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/thinking.md · keywords: Ollama thinking capability and reasoning controls · also: https://ollama.com/blog/thinking
- [statement] CLI controls from the launch blog: `--think` enables, `--think=false` disables, `--hidethinking` hides reasoning for scripting, and `/set think` / `/set nothink` toggle inside an interactive session. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-05-30) — https://ollama.com/blog/thinking · keywords: Ollama thinking capability and reasoning controls
- [statement] Current docs: `think` accepts true, false, null (model default), or a string from the model's `thinking.values`; numbers are unsupported and unsupported names fall back to the model default. Clients discover `values` and `default` from a top-level `thinking` object in /api/show; `values: [false]` means no thinking support, and a missing `thinking` object means no thinking metadata. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/thinking.md · keywords: Ollama thinking capability and reasoning controls
- [statement] Before the think switch shipped, Qwen3 on Ollama ignored `enable_thinking=False` and users had to append `/no_think` to prompts; a maintainer closed the issue on 2025-05-30 pointing to PR #10584 and the v0.9.0 release as the configurable switch. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/10809 · keywords: Ollama thinking capability and reasoning controls · also: https://ollama.com/blog/thinking
